## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Uppādanirodhavāra* (Ya 2.2.3) is a section of the *Yamaka*, the sixth book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Standing as the third subdivision of the process section (*pavattivāra*) of its chapter, it treats doctrinal categories under the combined perspective of their origination and cessation [Gal 2003; Ronkin, Early Buddhist Metaphysics]. As modern scholars note, the structural analysis across the process sections of the *Yamaka*—advancing through origination (*uppāda-vāra*), cessation (*nirodha-vāra*), and origination-cessation (*uppādanirodha-vāra*)—embodies an early Buddhist process metaphysics where phenomena are treated as dynamic occurrences rather than enduring entities [Gal 2003; Ronkin, Early Buddhist Metaphysics]. In this context, these sections mark an early textual occurrence of the technical term *khaṇa* subdivided into distinct moments of origination (*uppādakkhaṇa*) and cessation (*bhaṅgakkhaṇa*), forming an important milestone in the Abhidhamma theory of momentariness [Gal 2003; Ronkin, Early Buddhist Metaphysics]. SuttaCentral records one modern translation of the text [SuttaCentral].
